forecast-period.text: A trough over the northwest will weaken today with a high pressure ridge south of the state expected to move north and hover over SA during Monday. A cold front is forecast to pass over the southeast early Tuesday, then quickly followed by a high pressure system that is expected to pass to the south of the state later Tuesday and on Wednesday, maintaining a ridge over the state.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and isolated thunderstorms over the west, with showers extending to central and eastern parts during the day. Maximum temperatures below average, tending well below average in the north. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Possible morning fog in the far west. Mostly dry, though a slight chance of an isolated shower or thunderstorm over the far north. Maximum temperatures below average. Light winds, tending northwesterly in the south during the day.

Showers about the southern agricultural area, clearing during the day. Maximum temperatures below average. Northwesterly winds in the south, tending south to southwesterly during the day. South to southeasterly winds in the north.

text.p: Dry. Maximum temperatures below average in the east, gradient to above average in the west. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: Less than 2 mm across the far northeast and agricultural areas, increasing to 2 to 5 mm in the southeast and the Mount Lofty Ranges. 2 to 10 mm elsewhere, increasing to 10 to 15 mm in the North West Pastoral district with isolated falls reaching up to 30 mm.
